title: Halcyon Retail — inference savings heatmap (draft)
summary: Working draft: before/after savings analysis for Halcyon Retail after applying Redwood Optimize recommendations (batching, mix-and-match model routing, and KV-prefix caching). This doc synthesizes spreadsheet outputs and converts them into a reader-friendly heatmap and prioritized actions. Numbers are preliminary and derived from Halcyon's Q3 request logs (anonymized).
baseline_snapshot:
Baseline (current customer setup):
- Avg qps: 18 sustained (peak 42)
- Workload: 72% short chat completions (~80 tokens), 28% long generation (~1200 tokens)
- Model in use: halcyon-prod-13b (FP16) across a single region
- Current bill estimate: $98,400/month (inferred from tokens + infra allocation)
- Observed 99th latency: 620ms for short, 2.6s for long generations
- No prefix/KV cache in production; limited batching (per request level).
optimize_changes:
Applied Redwood Optimize recommendations (spreadsheet scenario A):
1) Introduce prefix KV cache for 60% of short-chat traffic (templates & product prompts).
2) Enable continuous batching with 60ms max latency budget for short completions.
3) Route low-cost best-effort queries to a quantized 7B variant (mistral-7b-q4_0) when safety checks pass.
4) Keep long-tail long generations on 13B FP16 but enable dynamic batching groups of size up to 8.
5) Implement A/B rollout (10% traffic) for new routing rules before full rollout.
Spreadsheet scenario file: halcyon-optimize-scenarios-v1 (linked in spreadsheet_refs).
projected_savings:
Month-1 projection (post A/B ramp to 100% over 6 weeks):
- Token/infra cost reduction: 31% (~$30,500/month)
- End-to-end unit cost (short comps): down 46% per request
- Overall monthly bill: ~$67,900/month (estimated)
- Latency: p50 unchanged, p95 for short comps improves to ~280ms; p99 target requires further tuning for cache misses.
- Qualitative: slight increase in variance for long-tail requests during batching windows; no major quality regression observed in sample evals.
sensitivity_notes:
Key sensitivities and assumptions:
- Traffic mix shift: if short-chat share drops below 50%, savings fall to ~18%.
- Cache hit-rate assumption: 60% hit used; if actual hit-rate <40%, savings reduce by ~40% of projected.
- Quantized 7B quality: assumed acceptable for 40% of low-risk prompts; we flagged 12 prompt categories that require human review.
- Peak concurrency: savings realized in steady state; during sudden spikes, autoscaler add-ons may add incremental cost.
- Exchange rate & cloud GPU pricing volatility not modeled; spreadsheet has toggles for +/-15% price sensitivity.
heatmap_methodology:
Heatmap generation notes:
- X axis: request token length buckets (0-128, 129-512, 513-2048)
- Y axis: frequency percentiles (p50, p75, p90, p99) by request type (short chat, long gen, rerank).
- Cell value: delta in $/1M requests (before - after).
- Colors: deep-green = savings >$400, pale-yellow = savings under $50, red = negative impact.
- Data sources: anonymized access logs (Q3), infra billing exports, Redwood Optimize simulation engine outputs.
- Caveats: heatmap smooths across hourly spikes; we include separate hourly-peak overlay in spreadsheet.
recommendations: Run a gated A/B rollout (10% -> 50% -> 100%) with automatic rollback on quality/regression alerts
Prioritize implementation of KV-prefix cache for the top 15 prompt templates (expected 60-70% hit rate)
Enable continuous batching for short completions with 60ms latency budget and monitor tail latency closely
Deploy quantized 7B routing only for low-risk prompt categories and keep 13B for safety-critical flows
Add a weekly dashboard for cache hit-rate, cost per 1k requests, and per-route latency p95/p99
